question: The tendency of formation of basic oxide _____ when we are shifting down in a group.
solution:
The correct answer is__** increases.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **basic oxide** is formed when an element combines with oxygen and produces a** basic solution** when dissolved in water. 
 
• The trend of basic oxide formation in a group is** dependent** on the** size of the atom** and its** valence electrons.**
 
• As we **move down** a group, the** atomic size increases**, and the valence electrons are located farther from the nucleus.
 
• The increase in atomic size and **distance of valence electrons** from the nucleus leads to a **decrease** in the effective nuclear charge experienced by the valence electrons.
 
• As a result, the valence electrons are **less strongly attracted** to the nucleus, making it easier for them to form a basic oxide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **atomic number increases** moving left to right across a period and subsequently so does the** effective nuclear charge.**
 
• As a result, the **atomic radii decreas**e and the** nucleus exerts a stronger attraction** on the outside electrons as one moves from l**eft to right** across a period.
 
• The number of **full electron shells rises** as one moves down a group in the periodic table.
 
• The orbitals of valence electrons in a group are now farther from the nucleus, but they still have the** same effective nuclear charge.**
 
• The atomic radii are therefore** larger** and the** nucleus exerts less force **on the outside electrons.
